title: Secret Sauce
status_note: In daily use across my projects; five commits in, the lint rules still change weekly.
oneliner: My house design system: two inks on plaster, with tools that enforce it.
role: I designed the system, drew the Stem 7 pixel font, and built the asset generator and the automated art director.

hero.alt: Contact sheet of generated brand assets: card, banner, splash, title and icons

media.alt: Plate sample in the Secret Sauce style
media.caption: A plate: cobalt and vermilion on plaster, vermilion used once.
The component sheet that every project pulls its tokens from.
Social cards come out of the same generator, not out of a template tool.

body: This whole portfolio is dressed in it. Secret Sauce is two inks, cobalt and vermilion, on plaster, with vermilion allowed once per surface and no gradients, glows or rounded cards.

A system only holds if something enforces it, so sauce-lint acts as an automated art director that flags a page when it breaks the rules, and sauce make generates cards, banners, splash screens and favicons from the same tokens. Stem 7, a pixel face drawn on the grid of my mark, sets the type.
What I learned: rules written as lint checks survive; rules written as prose get argued with.

title: The fridge
status_note: The library is built and labelled; the remixes are experiments, and the labels are machine-assisted, not audited.
oneliner: A 1,536-image inspiration library I can search by facet and remix from.
role: I collected the pins, designed the label taxonomy, read the contact sheets, and wrote TASTE.md from what the library shows.

hero.alt: Contact sheet of pinned inspiration images grouped by cluster

media.alt: One geometric mark rendered in six kitchens
media.caption: One mark, six kitchens: a remix built from the geometric-marks cluster.
Cozy-pixel remix, made after studying what the saved pixel scenes share.
A plotter-math remix: a flow field drawn as pen lines.

spec.label: remix folders
spec.source: subfolders of remixes/ (includes rejects and src)

body: The fridge is where my taste is written down: 1,536 saved images, each with faceted labels for use, style and mood, so I can ask for all the iso cutaways or every terminal HUD and get an answer.

I labelled by reading contact sheets, then wrote TASTE.md, a plain reading of what the pins show, including that the biggest buckets are feed noise and the hero-dense styles are where the taste lives. The remixes follow Steal Like an Artist: study many sources, transform, and keep the lineage.
What I learned: counting a collection is the fastest way to find out what you actually like versus what you merely saved.

title: Pantry
status_note: Works for me on 61 links; a single-day build with no tests and no one else using it.
oneliner: A command-line database of permissive open-source software I might reuse.
role: I specced it and built the CLI so I can dump links fast and have licenses and activity looked up as evidence.

hero.alt: Pantry's searchable, filterable HTML table of saved projects

body: Pantry is one SQLite file and a CLI: paste links into an inbox, run one command, and every GitHub repo, model or site is stored with its license, activity and owner type fetched as evidence.

The point is sorting by what is safe to build on (permissive licenses, still maintained) rather than by hype, then rendering a searchable table. Re-adding a link merges notes and tags instead of duplicating.
What I learned: keeping capture to one paste is what makes a library like this actually get filled.

title: The workbench
status_note: Three side projects: the recipe manual is published, the corpus is captions-only (Whisper not started), the rack is designed with STLs, print status not recorded here.
oneliner: A shared-GPU recipe manual, a transcript corpus, and a 3D-printed rack.
role: I wrote the manual, set up the download and transcription pipeline, and modelled the rack in OpenSCAD.

hero.alt: Render of the assembled 10-inch rack in OpenSCAD

media.alt: Exploded view of the rack parts
media.caption: Exploded view: every part is a parametric OpenSCAD module.

media.alt: Front view of one rack bay
media.caption: One bay from the front, as modelled before slicing.

body: One RTX 3060 serves every project on my machine, so I wrote the RTX 3060 Recipe Manual: what fits in 12 GB, what runs together, and how to take turns without out-of-memory crashes.
Beside it sit a YouTube research corpus (463 videos catalogued, 380 with cleaned captions, audio queued for local Whisper) and a 10-inch rack for the home network, modelled in OpenSCAD with 61 STLs.
What I learned: boring infrastructure written down once saves every later session.
